Meeting Header
Date: 2026-07-22 10:30 AM UTC

Location: Zoom

Summary:
Quick kickoff / ignition for Maple Court Health's implementation of Redwood inference platform (hosted -> dedicated pilot runway). Cover scope, timeline, security checklist (SOC2, KMS, SSO), infra requirements (VPC peering, subnets), and next steps for runbook and perf benchmarks.

Topics:
- Goals and success criteria (pin latency, cost target, uptime slos)
- Deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Network & security: VPC peering, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Data retention, audit, and compliance
- Ramp plan: canary, pilot, scale to prod
- Benchmarks and integration checklist

Action Items (recap at end included as separate metadata): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, customer success, and Diego will be joining from solutions eng. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:12] Olivia Park: Olivia here, head of AI at Maple Court.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Samir, platform eng.
[00:17] Janelle Moore: Janelle, product ops.
[00:19] Ethan Ross: Ethan, security.
[00:21] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood, good to meet you all.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Great — objective for today is to align on the ignition plan, get the infra checklist completed, and set dates for the infra deep-dive. We'll also cover security docs — SOC2 and logging.
[00:40] Olivia Park: Sounds good. We're primarily interested in the dedicated path but want to validate hosted first for speed. Our initial goals are mean latency < 250ms 95th p99 maybe under 500ms? and cost per 1k tokens below the budget we set.
[01:02] Diego Alvarez: Good — for those numbers we usually recommend a small dedicated pool with auto-scaling and prefix caching, that way the KV cache helps with repeated prompts. Just to call out, KV cahce — sorry, kv cache — is key for prompt-heavy workflows.
[01:18] Samir Patel: Quick infra note: Maple Court runs in AWS us-east-1, we prefer VPC peering; we have strict egress controls so peering + private link is our usual pattern.
[01:34] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll need VPC peering details (CIDRs), and a KMS key ARN if you want customer-managed encryption. We have a private deployment option too if you need on-prem or air-gapped.
[01:48] Ethan Ross: Security — our checklist: SOC2 status, SAML/SSO integration, per-request audit logs retained 1 year, and key management. Curious what Redwood supports out of box.
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: We support SAML SSO via Okta, ADFS testing, RBAC via the console. Audit logs are available for dedicated and private — hosted has event logs but longer retention is an add-on. We can share our SOC2 pack; will toggle on the audit log export for your team during pilot.
[02:28] Janelle Moore: Timeline — we'd like a pilot live in 4 weeks, full roll to prod in 10 weeks, dependent on perf readouts. Is that realistic?
[02:40] Maya Chen: 4 weeks for a pilot is reasonable: week 1 infra and onboarding, week 2 basic integration & smoke tests, week 3 perf benching + canary, week 4 adjustments and go/no-go. The dedicated migration to follow after pilot based on traffic.
[02:58] Olivia Park: Our stakeholders: CTO and HIPAA compliance officer need to be in the loop — there may be additional sign-off steps around data residency. Not sure if Redwood does region-specific hosting in multiple regions yet.
[03:12] Diego Alvarez: We have hosted regions in us-east-1 and eu-west-1; private deployments can be brought into other regions or on-prem. We'll document region options in the runbook.
[03:28] Maya Chen: I'm going to walk through the runbook high level now — it's in the shared drive.
[03:34] Maya Chen: Section one: access & auth — how we onboard users, SSO setup notes, and role mapping for RBAC. Section two: infra — VPC peering steps, firewall rules, subnets, NAT. Section three: data flow and retention. Section four: perf benching and sample prompts.
[03:54] Samir Patel: On the VPC peering, do you require us to open any inbound? We tend to avoid inbound unless via private link.
[04:02] Diego Alvarez: For peering it's strictly internal routing, no public inbound. If you prefer private link we can discuss. For dedicated we often use a peered VPC with specific route tables.
[04:18] Ethan Ross: KMS — if we bring our own key, how is key usage audited? We need to show key usage logs in our KMS.
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: We don't hold your key; we integrate via KMS grants. Key usage is recorded in your cloud provider's KMS logs — we'll show how to tie those to our audit events. We'll capture request IDs in the audit trail.
[04:42] Janelle Moore: For the perf benchmarks, what traffic profile do you want? Short chatty requests vs long form generation?
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: Great question. Please provide both: 70% short-turn dialog under 128 tokens, 30% long form up to 1k tokens. We'll run both a latency-focused and throughput-focused test. I'll share the perf template.
[05:10] Maya Chen: Ok, next — integrations: you mentioned a pipeline that calls an internal reranker service post-generation. We recommend setting a canary route so you can compare responses and fall back to the previous infra if needed.
[05:24] Olivia Park: There's also PII gating before we send prompts out. We'll need to ensure we can redact at the client side and still have embeddings/metadata stored. Any gotchas?
[05:35] Diego Alvarez: Redaction at client side is fine. For embeddings we recommend hashing identifiers before embedding and using deterministic salt your side. Also note tokenization differences across model variants; we'll document which model families handle your prompt patterns best.
[05:55] Samir Patel: One thing: our legal team asked about data residency and purge policies. Can Redwood do scheduled purge for hosted logs?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Hosted can do log purges with the enterprise add-on. For dedicated/private you control storage retention directly. We'll put the retention options in the runbook with steps to enable automatic purge.
[06:16] Olivia Park: Let's talk about rollout plan: canary to 5% for 48 hours, then 25% 72 hours, then full. We want rollback triggers on error rate > 1% or latency spike > 2x. Can Redwood support automatic fallback?
[06:34] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we have built-in rollout policies. Canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant or previous model if SLOs breach. We'll show configuration in the console demo.
[06:50] Janelle Moore: Who's responsible for on-call during pilot?
[06:54] Maya Chen: Redwood provides a pilot support window — Diego and I will be on the initial on-call rotation. We can coordinate 24/7 coverage if needed once in prod under the SLA.
[07:06] Ethan Ross: Audit logs format — can we ingest them into our Splunk?
[07:10] Diego Alvarez: Yes, logs can be exported to a syslog endpoint or S3 which you can pull into Splunk. We'll include sample parsers.
[07:22] Olivia Park: Any items on quotas and rate limiting for pilot?
[07:27] Maya Chen: We'll provision a dedicated quota for your pilot to avoid noisy neighbor problems. We'll also provide throttling configs.
[07:35] Samir Patel: Cost modeling — can you share a sample cost sheet for the pilot and for a projected 10k reqs/day?
[07:41] Diego Alvarez: I'll share the cost model. Quick note: quantized model variants reduce vRAM and cost but sometimes degrade output slightly — tradeoff to test.
[07:55] Olivia Park: Ok if we start the infra deep-dive next Tuesday?
[07:58] Maya Chen: Next Tuesday 2026-07-28 works for us; calling that our infra design session.
[08:04] Janelle Moore: We'll invite the compliance officer to that meeting.
[08:07] Olivia Park: Great.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Recap of immediate deliverables: 1) I'll send the runbook and perf template today, 2) Diego will send the benchmark checklist and sample results, 3) Samir to share VPC details and KMS by 7/29, 4) Schedule infra deep-dive for 7/28.
[08:28] Diego Alvarez: One more technical note — model pinning during rollout is important: you can pin to a quantized variant or fallback cheaper family. Also, the runtime supports efficient KV caching and prefix caching, but you need to enable session affinity for best hit rates.
[08:47] Samir Patel: Session affinity — is that sticky IP or token-based?
[08:51] Diego Alvarez: It's token/session-based via our routing layer, not IP sticky. We'll include config snippet in the runbook.
[09:05] Maya Chen: Any blockers from the customer's side?
[09:08] Samir Patel: We need internal sign-off and the compliance review; otherwise, no technical blockers.
[09:14] Ethan Ross: I'll review the SOC2 pack and get back with specific questions, likely within 72 hours.
[09:20] Olivia Park: Fine. One last note — our data team wants to test reranking latency too; can that be included in perf?
[09:27] Diego Alvarez: Yes, include reranker calls in the traffic profile. We'll also test end-to-end 3-step pipeline.
[09:36] Maya Chen: OK, we'll pause there and leave time for any loose questions.
[09:40] Janelle Moore: Quick ops question — who uploads the service account credentials for the initial setup?
[09:45] Samir Patel: I'll do it, and I'll coordinate with Diego on the required IAM policy.
[09:50] Diego Alvarez: I'll send the minimal IAM policy and a sample CloudFormation snippet later today.
[09:58] Olivia Park: Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the runbook and links.
[10:05] (crosstalk)
[10:10] Maya Chen: End meeting.

(Transcript ends — total recording length 62:05)
